lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Make sure the LinkedIn text links to your actual profile URL.
items.because: The example-domain address may be anonymized for this review.

items.says: Remove the date of birth and nationality for most US applications.
items.because: They usually do not help assess qualifications and disclose personal information unnecessarily.

items.says: Clarify whether the MBA is completed or give the correct expected date.
items.because: The listed end date is June 2025, so the degree status must be accurate for the version sent.

items.says: Consider adding a concentration, relevant coursework, or another distinguishing MBA detail.
items.because: Such detail may add value for the target roles.

items.says: Define whether the 35% conversion increase is relative or in percentage points, and give its baseline, period, and scope.
items.because: The result needs clearer definitions and substantiation.

items.says: Explain how the flow change was isolated from other factors.
items.because: “After replacing” implies causation.

items.says: Clarify how the checkout flow for all merchants relates to the onboarding pilot.
items.because: The two flow claims could be distinct initiatives, rollout stages, or overlapping descriptions.

items.says: Clarify what you personally produced or coordinated.
items.because: The bullet describes cross-functional work without making your contribution precise.

items.says: Explain what “two weeks ahead of plan” refers to.
items.because: The shipped result and schedule claim need to be easy to verify.

items.says: Explain the data, assumptions, and currency behind the $1.1 million annual-loss estimate.
items.because: The basis for the estimate is unclear.

items.says: Clarify your role in the roadmap decision.
items.because: The claim should not overstate your influence.

items.says: Specify what counted as a ticket and how the queue reduction was measured.
items.because: The operational figures need clearer definitions.

items.says: Show the effect of the triage work on users or the business, or reconsider its space.
items.because: Ticket volume may be less compelling than the measured product changes.

items.says: Pair the opt-in comparison with what it found or remove it as a standalone bullet.
items.because: It describes a method but reads as incomplete without a result.

items.says: Address self-selection bias in the opt-in comparison.
items.because: Merchants who opted in may differ from those who did not.

items.says: Define “time to first payment,” the comparison period, and the pilot-region figure.
items.because: The result needs clearer definitions.

items.says: Clarify whether all 2,300 merchants were exposed to the redesign.
items.because: The scope of the pilot result is unclear.

items.says: Clarify how the onboarding initiative differs from the checkout-flow work.
items.because: The checkout bullet says all merchants, while this bullet describes a pilot region.

items.says: Excluding weather-delayed shipments does not establish that late deliveries were cut.
items.because: It changes the on-time calculation rather than necessarily improving underlying delivery performance.

items.says: Explain the metric definition and any operational change that produced the result.
items.because: Otherwise the claim risks sounding like metric manipulation.

items.says: Add the period and explain how pick errors were counted.
items.because: Those details would make the 30% result clearer.

items.says: Explain how slotting changes and picker retraining contributed to the outcome.
Fix the present-tense “prepares.”
items.because: The Crestline role ended in 2023.

items.says: Substantiate a concrete result or reconsider whether the bullet is worth the space.
items.because: It describes recurring responsibilities rather than an outcome.

items.says: Explain how the annual 1,800-hour saving was calculated and whether it was measured or projected.
Distinguish your rollout and training contribution from the team’s overall result.
Clarify the project’s current status and whether the app is still active.
items.because: The project is listed as ongoing.

items.says: Clarify the team size and what you personally owned as Product Lead.
items.because: The title and scale of the results invite questions about team scope.

items.says: Clarify whether “launched to 3,100 students” means availability, registrations, or actual reach.
Define the first-year period and how the nine tonnes were tracked.
Give the measurement window for weekly active user growth.
Establish whether the growth from 400 to 1,150 supports a connection to reminders.
items.because: The growth must be attributable enough to support that connection.

items.says: Explain who was interviewed and what the 60 interviews revealed.
State the period behind the 95% figure and how staff cover shifts were counted.
Clarify your role in setting up the system versus the dining halls’ role in operating it.
Add a concrete deliverable, decision, or outcome from the working sessions.
items.because: The bullet communicates activity but not what changed and may be lower-value than the more specific bullets.

items.says: Replace the passive construction with what you personally did.
items.because: The passive wording obscures your contribution.

items.says: Clarify what was changed, how the four clinics were selected, and what “adopted” means in practice.
Add a measurable result if available.
items.because: A change in intake time or completion would make the impact easier to assess.

items.says: The merchant-onboarding result is misplaced and duplicates the Harbor Payments result.
items.because: The same 2,300-merchants and first-payment result appears under a regional hospital project, making it look like a copy-paste error.

items.says: Support the broad product skills with specific examples and methods, especially A/B testing.
items.because: Interviewers may ask about experiment design and statistical interpretation.
